item.title: Ill Bloom Crypto Wallet Drains and BlackCat Negotiator Sentencing
item.content:encoded:
Attackers Exploit 'Ill Bloom' Vulnerability to Drain $3.1 Million From Cryptocurrency Wallets — Must Read

Coinspect says attackers exploited the “Ill Bloom” weak-randomness flaw in some older or lesser-known crypto wallets to drain about $3.1 million from 431 wallets, with more funds potentially exposed. Users should check public addresses at illbloom.org and, if matched, move funds to a brand-new wallet with a freshly generated recovery phrase.

  • Coinspect disclosed a crypto wallet flaw called Ill Bloom, where some wallet software generated recovery phrases with weak randomness that attackers could work out.
  • Coinspect confirmed a coordinated sweep on May 27 that drained about $3.1 million from 431 wallets, with roughly $2 million more moving from exposed wallets since then.
  • Coinspect says wallets created on hardware devices are not affected, and most mainstream software wallets are not affected, while the real risk is with older or lesser-known mobile wallets, some dating back to 2018.
  • The affected weak phrases can expose funds across every chain they control, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Rootstock, Tron, and Polygon addresses traced by Coinspect.
  • Coinspect advises users to check public wallet addresses at illbloom.org and, if there is a match, create a brand-new wallet with a brand-new recovery phrase and move funds there.

Ransomware Negotiator Gets 70 Months in Prison for Aiding BlackCat Attacks — Should Read

Former ransomware negotiator Angelo Martino was sentenced to 70 months in U.S. prison for secretly helping BlackCat operators extort his own clients by sharing their confidential negotiation and insurance details. Prosecutors said he also helped target additional victims with two other cybersecurity professionals, while authorities have seized $10 million in illicit assets.

  • Angelo Martino, a 41-year-old former ransomware negotiator from Land O'Lakes, Florida, was sentenced to 70 months in U.S. prison for conspiring with BlackCat ransomware operators to extort multiple victims.
  • Federal prosecutors said Martino worked as a negotiator for five ransomware victims while secretly giving BlackCat attackers confidential information about the victims' negotiation positions, strategies, and insurance policy limits.
  • Martino pleaded guilty in April to one count of conspiring to interfere with interstate commerce through extortion.
  • Martino was also accused of colluding with Ryan Goldberg and Kevin Martin to deploy BlackCat ransomware against multiple U.S. victims between April 2023 and November 2023.
  • The Justice Department said law enforcement has seized $10 million in assets from Martino, including digital currency, vehicles, a food truck, and a luxury fishing boat.
